source.note: The plan's source (a Quaternius static bamboo on poly.pizza) is behind a Cloudflare challenge; this is Kenney's Nature Kit (the same sha256-pinned zip as mushroom-red). The kit's only bamboo members are `crops_bambooStageA` (three short culms, 0.55 units) and `crops_bambooStageB` (the same three culms grown taller, 0.89 units): a farm-crop growth stage with no leaves, three segmented hexagonal culms each. One lone crop reads as three posts, so the entry builds a grove clump from kit pieces: StageB plus two StageA copies placed by `ingest.attach` (offsets and turns chosen so that no two of the nine culms touch), giving nine culms of three heights in a 3.3 x 3.1 m footprint. Height 6 m: Japanese grove bamboo (madake, moso) stands 4-8 m in a managed grove; the tallest culms reach 6 m and the short ones 3.5 m. The culms are stylized thick (about 0.5 m across at this size, real madake is 0.1-0.15 m); uniform scaling cannot fix that, so it is a chunky low-poly clump, for mid and background. The alternative (OpenGameArt free-bamboo-v1 by yughues, CC0) has thin culms and leaves but ships as a 7z with alpha-card leaves, which the pipeline cannot unpack and the flat cel look would turn into solid quads. Colours on noon (no green): a pale cane, skin shading to iris, the same trunk pair as tree-palm. No leaves, so nothing is double-sided; kept faceted (`smooth: false`) like the other Kenney Nature Kit pieces. Static, no clips.
